title: When Good Intentions Lead To Bad Judgement In Israel

sense.text: “but when ye entered, ye defiled my land”. Israel always got their hand in some crap. God gave us that plentiful land, and when we went into it we defiled it and made his heritage an abomination.

“The priests said not, Where is the Lord?” The same thing is going on today with these Christian churches, Christianity under the Roman Catholics. They all the same. They all demonic. “and they that handle the law knew me not”. The men supposed to be teaching the law and preaching to the flock don't know the Lord. They're not keeping the laws. They're about to celebrate Christmas, teaching that it's Jesus Christ's birthday, when December 25th is nowhere in the Bible. Nowhere were we Israelites told to celebrate Christmas, but these churches teach it all around the world.

Catch Deacon Asaph's Friday Night Raw class on Christmas. Out in the Solomon Islands we saw a big tree in front of a bank, and Bishop and Captain Yidden did a commentary striking that thing down. In Papua New Guinea we saw a big tree too. Everywhere we go we see that damn tree, the idol. People worship it or call it celebrating. Our people don't teach, abide by, or apply the laws; they don't even want to hear the laws anymore.

“the pastors also transgressed against me, and the prophets prophesied by Baal, and walked after things that do not profit.” They're following Satan, not what God said. These churches always have a new gimmick, a new scheme, a new thing to entertain everybody. They don't know God. It ain't about teaching the Bible, how Christ looks, who our people are, or what they're supposed to do before Christ returns. God set us up right now to do that work.

“Her priests have violated my law, and have profaned mine holy things”. They put no difference between holy and profane. They come up with all type of foolishness, follow it, and tell the people to follow it too. “neither have they shewed difference between the unclean and the clean, and have hid their eyes from my sabbaths”. Christmas, Father's Day, Mother's Day, Easter, Thanksgiving, First Lady Day, Building Day—all type of foolishness. They're following Satan to the fullest in them buildings. They don't know Christ, and they're teaching our people not to know Christ, to stay away from him. Satan has to gather his two-thirds while we're out here gathering the one-third.

“Her princes in the midst thereof are like wolves ravening the prey”. They're hunting people down and tearing them up, ripping their souls out of them, keeping them in sin, darkness, and wickedness. People are waiting to hear the words out of the Bible, but the pastors with the mic are singing, acting, entertaining, not feeding the people the word of God. “to shed blood, and to destroy souls, to get dishonest gain.” They're playing games with the church.

That older man is supposed to be an example to the young men, but he's dancing like he's back in the club partying. Nobody has their Bibles open. Our people aren't learning God. These antics teach them to get away and stay away from God. This is serious work; we have a big job on our hands.

“Your iniquities have turned away these things, and your sins have withholden good things from you.” Our sins turn good things away from us. That's why God ain't blessing us like we're supposed to be blessed. Our people are full of idolatry, lies, fornication, adultery, reveling, whining and dancing, and celebrating fake holidays nowhere in the Bible. We have to come out of that mindset.

“For among my people are found wicked men”. They lie in wait, laying traps for our people. “they set a trap, they catch men.” “As a cage is full of birds, so are their houses full of deceit”. The church houses are full of deceit. There's no truth in there, nobody bringing the people back to who they are and their greatness. They're arguing about stupidness, about the Trinity. All right, the three is one—now what? They're not keeping any laws. A brother was arguing about the breakdown of a candy cane. All this foolishness keeps us away from our God. “therefore they are become great, and waxen rich.”

“yea, they overpass the deeds of the wicked”. They overpass the deeds of the Roman Catholic Church and all these other wicked entities. They're overpassing the clubs with what they're doing in church. “they judge not the cause, the cause of the fatherless”. They're not judging matters or the right of the needy. People go to the churches to be a whoremonger, commit adultery, make money, and find women they can post up and lay up with and have a good crib to stay in.

These antics pull our people away from God, the Bible, and understanding who they are and what they're supposed to do before Christ returns. Grace is a small amount of time to get yourself right before Christ comes back; they're abusing it with sin, wickedness, and evil. Look at the woman in the polka dots on the mic, the DJ, the MC, with her head not covered, while the man dances. We have to stop playing these games.

The Lord is sending us into every city, state, island, country, and continent to fix this and give his people a chance to return before they're devoured with this evil. It's on us men to stand up, learn, study, apply, and go teach. None of these schools are hangouts, biker clubs, motorcycle clubs, or caddy clubs. Our schools are built to bring our people back to the heavenly Father in righteousness, keeping the commandments as written.

precepts.why: “It is better to hear the rebuke of the wise” than “the song of fools.” Ain't nothing wrong with glorifying the Lord with good righteous music. We have righteous music in Original Royalty. But gospel music singing to Satan, songs to Cesare Borgia, songs full of emotion and feelings that don't bring our people back to who they are—that song is worthless.

sense.text: “Every plant, which my heavenly Father hath not planted, shall be rooted up.” All these evil pastors and evil congregations in Christianity, if they don't get right, they're going to be plucked up, rooted up, thrown out.

“they be blind leaders of the blind.” These churches are full of women usurping authority over the men, and the men are weak. It shouldn't be a weak Israelite on this earth. Knowing the lies we've been taught, we should all be standing up strong, battling and getting our people right. Everything on this earth right now is out of course. God is depending on us, trusting us to use his words to get his people back in order.

Benjamin is getting touched this time; Judah had his turn with his foolery in these churches and will get his turn too. All this dancing and shaking hips in the damn church, full of women and kids—where are the real men? We have to get ourselves together. “And if the blind lead the blind, both shall fall into the ditch.” Both of them are going to fall.

“Having a form of godliness”. So a lot of them have a form of godliness. “but denying the power thereof”. They denying the power that God give them. This is the power he give all of us. You understand? He give us the power and they deny the power. They hate the Bible. They hate us. They hate God through their actions. Not through their words, but through their actions. Show you that they hate God. They hate the Bible and they hate God people.

“from such turn away.” But such like that, y'all better get away from them. You Christians that's in them churches, y'all better get away from these demons. You better get away from the demons and the ones in y'all's that just came out of that garbage. All praise to you. All praise. May the most high bless you cuz you leaving that foolishness and you coming into this truth and you learning and finding out what you need to do before that last day, before Christ come or before you leave this earth. One of the two.

“For of this sort are they which creep into houses”. That's what they going on in the churches. That's why he think he whining and dancing like that. Whining and dancing. He trying to turn the women on. Gyrating. What they calling the church is gyrating. That's what it is. He gyrating in the church.

“which creep into houses, and lead captive silly women”. That's what's happening. All a bunch of silly women in that building. They are screaming and laughing and dancing, but they have no understanding who they are and the trouble that's coming down the pipeline. They don't understand Jacob troubles is coming. Things are about to get rough. You understand? Things are about to get really rough out here. Trump been in office one year and he turned it up this whole year. He got three more years to go. Let's get our minds right, y'all. “laden with sins”. These silly women that's laden with sin. “led away with divers lusts”.

“Ever learning, and never able to come to the knowledge of the truth.” Ever learning, but they listen, they hear us. They hear us in the streets. They see us on these different social media outlets. They see us. They hear us, but they never come to the truth. They never be able to come to the truth because Satan got a stronghold on them. You understand?

“Now as Jannes and Jambres withstood Moses, so do these also resist the truth”. Them sorcerers, the witches, the warlocks, how they resist us back then, have they resist God back then? That's what they doing today. Them same demons is back on this earth again, resisting this truth, fighting against the word of God, fighting against change. You know what's crazy about our people? Our people want change, but they don't want to change.

“men of corrupt minds”. Men of corrupt minds. “reprobate”. They void understanding. “concerning the faith.” Concerning Christ, concerning his truth, and concerning them getting themselves together.
“Yea, and all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution.” So us that's going to live godly, we going to suffer persecution.

“But evil men and seducers shall wax worse and worse, deceiving, and being deceived.” They deceiving and they being deceived. You understand? They're going to wax worse and worse because Satan got to get together his two thirds. And the Most High is have us down here getting together to one third. You understand? Through righteous leaders. Through righteous leaders. I'm going to say it again. Through righteous leaders who leading us up the right path. You understand? Who setting a great example that we all should be following. You understand? That's the men the most high sent back to this earth to get us all back in order. So we need to be following. We need to be following. But in that Christianity and that wickedness out there, they deceiving people and they be deceived they self as well.

You can't make this up. You can't make this up. Look at the man. Look at the man. Look at the man run up like he's all right. One man and 50 women in there. Hold on. Stop that. That's the foolishness we dealing with. One man and 50 women.

You know what he's saying? Hold up. You know he said he under the blood. What that mean, right? You know what that mean? He can sin. He can sin. He under the blood of Christ. He can sin. He could do evil. He ain't got to give account for nothing. Only thing he got to do is call on the name of the Lord and he going to get the kingdom of heaven because he under the blood. That's what he's saying to them people.

He talking about put the blood on his face just like a makeup. You understand? I'm telling you these Christians, man, I'm telling you. They destroyed, man. They destroyed. We have a heavy job to do, y'all. Dealing with them. He talking about put the blood on his face like just like it's makeup.

They get that from Colossian 1 and 20 talking about he under the blood of Christ. You understand? That's not for us to sin. That's for us to get ourselves together. You understand? Christ died for our sins. For us to get oursel together, not for us to keep sinning. You see what coming with that cross?

God house turned to a house of thieves. You understand what I'm saying? A den of thieves. That's what God house turned to. A clubhouse, a party house. Come in there and feel good and give your money and you go and you evil for the rest of the week. You go there, you supposed to go there to learn.
“The law of truth was in his mouth, and iniquity was not found in his lips”. “and did turn many away from iniquity.” That's what the priest is supposed to be doing.

“For the priest’s lips should keep knowledge”. The priest should teach the people how to get themselves together. “and they should seek the law at his mouth”. We should go to the priest or pastor to learn God's laws: stop eating pork, stop celebrating fake holidays, get your house in order, do the righteous things God said, and keep the high holy days. “for he is the messenger of the Lord of hosts.” He's supposed to teach you to wear fringes and keep the Sabbath holy—not Sunday, the Sabbath day. That's what they should teach in these buildings.

“Let the woman learn in silence with all subjection.” That woman in the church is supposed to be learning in silence with all subjection. On their women's day she's telling the men to stand up and act like men, calling them weak jellybacks. The man stands there looking stupid in the face.

“But I suffer not a woman to teach, nor to usurp authority over the man”. She has no business in that building talking to the men like that, no rights to talk to any man like that. She's usurping authority, and God ain't going to play with that lady if she doesn't repent. This whole earth is out of order: women leading and preaching in the churches, talking down to the men, and the men clapping, swinging their arms, weak and feminine.

“but to be in silence.” She's supposed to shut her black lips. Don't listen to the black woman. Soon as you give her a little inch, she's going with it, disrespecting the man, telling him to stand up, calling him weak and a jellyback. Some of these men are jellybacks in there, but she's still not supposed to be doing that according to the scriptures.

So they use that as an escape route or they use that as a backup plan just in case when things fall apart they can say, well, I had good intentions.

Definition read aloud: 'Intentions are invisible. Outcomes are not. You can't measure someone's intentions. Only their actions.'

Only their actions. You only could measure their what? Actions. Their what? Their actions. So when men out here and they talking about, well, I had good intentions. I meant good. I tried to do the right. No. Your actions going to show what you really meant. You understand? Your intentions is nothing but words in the air. You understand? Your actions show if you serious about doing it or not or serious about getting it done or not. Don't say you meant good. I had good intentions. That was an escape route for you to do the evil, for you to do the foolishness. You understand? Good intentions is bad judgment. You understand? Good intentions is bad judgment.

Definition read aloud: 'Cognitive dissonance. We tend to judge ourselves by our intentions. I meant well.'

I meant well. I meant to do the right thing.

Definition read aloud: 'But we judge others by their actions. They messed up.'

So you judging yourself by your good intentions, but you judging the next person by their actions. You see how hypocritical that is? I judge you by your actions by I'm judging myself by my good intentions, my good will, or I meant to do the right thing.

Definition read aloud: 'Moral licensing. Sometimes having good intentions makes people feel justified in doing questionable things.'

Doing wrong things. Doing wrong things. It could be a mask for control, ego, or fear. They lie to themselves. They lie to themselves. Maybe it's not so good after all.

See, that's what we do a lot of times. We give oursel excuses in life, man, to say, 'Oh, I meant good. That was a good intention.' But in the end, your actions really show what you meant. You understand? Your action really describe what you meant. Cuz even though you say you meant good, you got to have evil intentions, evil thoughts. But you disguise it under a good intention. You understand? So good intentions is bad judgment 90% of the time. You understand?

See, most people that do bad things still consider themselves to be good people.

Replayed video: 'Because when you assume your good intentions absolve you of accountability, you don't correct yourself. You justify yourself.'

You don't fix yourself to get better. You don't stay trying to get better. You stay doing the same foolishness because why? You meant good. You meant good. I meant good. I try to help. But the real results are you fail. You're lacking accountability. You never fix it cuz you never held yourself accountable for getting things done. You never held yourself accountable for doing whatever task, job, whatever you supposed to complete it. You just use that I had good intentions for an escape route for you to do it again next time. You understand? Just in case you need that for your backup, you could go to the I had good intentions escape route.

Your good intentions may not be good enough. That's what it go back to. You know what I'm saying? We got to start examining ourselves and really see what we doing. Are we really serious about it? Are we really applying oursel to it or are we just using it for escape route for us to do more foolishness in whatever office we have or whatever job task we have or whatever we supposed to be doing. You understand what I'm saying? And I see that happening a lot. That's why I wanted to touch on that because people use I had good intentions a lot of time for BS. You understand what I'm saying? For them to just run around and play games and give them time to do more foolishness and not taking accountability, not being responsible, not being disciplined or trustworthy that we could depend on you, having that dependency. We know we could call on you cuz you're going to get it done or we going to look at you and just say this guy always got excuses. He always say he meant good. He always say he had good intentions. We got to stop this.

“now therefore hearken thou unto the voice of the words of the Lord.” God gave Saul instructions. He remembered Amalek standing in Israel's way when we came up from Egypt. “Now go and smite Amalek, and utterly destroy all that they have”. Go over there and slay them, utterly destroy them. “but slay both man and woman, infant and suckling, ox and sheep, camel and ass.” Everything over there. Slay everything.
“two hundred thousand footmen, and ten thousand men of Judah.” Two hundred thousand footmen. That's how many Saul gathered.

“And he took Agag the king of the Amalekites alive”. God told him to destroy and slay everything—men, women, children, animals—but he kept the king. “But Saul and the people spared Agag”. God told him one thing and he did something else. He saved the best sheep, oxen, fatlings, lambs, the best of everything. “and would not utterly destroy them”. That wasn't the path he was supposed to go on. He was supposed to slay and destroy everything the Most High told him to destroy.

“I have performed the commandment of the Lord.” Now he lied. Besides not doing what God told him, he's putting sin on top of sin. “What meaneth then this bleating of the sheep in mine ears”. What the hell am I hearing sheep bleating for back there? Why am I hearing this noise if you killed everything like you were supposed to? “and the lowing of the oxen which I hear?”

“for the people spared the best of the sheep and of the oxen, to sacrifice unto the Lord thy God”. Did the Lord tell him to do that? No. He's talking about sparing the good to sacrifice to the Lord, trying to use his evil intent for a good intention.

“Stay, and I will tell thee what the Lord hath said to me this night.” Stay here; let me tell you what God told me to tell you. “When thou wast little in thine own sight”. Samuel took Saul back to when he first became king, reminding him of the things he had to do.

“Hath the Lord as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of the Lord?” I don't give a damn about no animal sacrifice. I need you to obey what I told you to do. I told you to go kill everything. I ain't ask you to sacrifice nothing or bring offerings. That was your job, task, and duty, and you didn't do it. I'd rather you obey me than bring them damn offerings and sacrifices I ain't tell you to bring.

“Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams.” That's what people don't realize. He knew those sacrifices weren't going to be around forever anyway. It's better to obey what he said than bring some damn sacrifices.

“For rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft”. “and stubbornness is as iniquity and idolatry.” “Because thou hast rejected the word of the Lord, he hath also rejected thee from being king.” Now the Lord doesn't want Saul to be king anymore. He's taking his reign from him.

“I have sinned”. Now he wants to confess, try to be clean and become innocent after disobeying a straight order from God. Was he sincere? No. He would have obeyed from the beginning. He tried to use good intentions to cover the evil he did. “because I feared the people, and obeyed their voice.” That's some evil crap. He's lying. If you fear the Lord, you're going to listen to the Lord. What the hell are you listening to the people for if you fear the Lord?
“And also the Strength of Israel will not lie nor repent”. The Strength of Israel is the Most High.

“Bring ye hither to me Agag the king of the Amalekites.” Bring that damn king, bring that Amalekite here. Where have you got him? Go get him. “Surely the bitterness of death is past.” Agag thought he was in a good place because of what Saul told him: don't worry, we'll take care of you. Surely you aren't going to kill me now, because the king told me you wouldn't put me to death.

“As thy sword hath made women childless, so shall thy mother be childless among women.” “And Samuel hewed Agag in pieces before the Lord in Gilgal.” Samuel did what the Lord told Saul to do from the beginning. He put that damn demon, that Amalekite, to death. Samuel had to do it. Samuel had to put the blade to him.

precepts.why: “Talk no more so exceeding proudly; let not arrogancy come out of your mouth”. “for the Lord is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed.” It ain't about what your mouth says or your good deeds. He don't give a damn about that. Your actions prove who you are, what type of man you are. If you can't be about your word, you won't be taken seriously. God gives you your reward from your actions.

sense.text:
“but Diotrephes, who loveth to have the preeminence among them, receiveth us not.” “prating against us with malicious words”. He's talking against the leaders, the elders, Peter and them, the men who helped set him up. Now he's highheaded, highminded, sitting on his high horse. He's the HNC, talking crap to the men who set him up as an elder of the school. I don't care if they're the damn disciples of Christ; I don't care if they walked with Christ; you're in my church. That's how he's talking.

“and not content therewith”. He's not content being the leader over there. “neither doth he himself receive the brethren, and forbiddeth them that would, and casteth them out of the church.” He doesn't want the apostles coming into the church, and he doesn't want the brothers receiving them either. If you go out there to see them because they walked with Christ, don't come back in my building. These same demons are back on this earth, prideful and arrogant.

“Wherefore, if I come, I will remember his deeds which he doeth”. Those malicious words against the leaders, refusing the brethren and throwing out the ones who would receive them—that's what he'll remember.

“Beloved, follow not that which is evil, but that which is good.” Don't follow that evil. Turn around and do the right thing; follow what's good. “He that doeth good is of God: but he that doeth evil hath not seen God.” Even with fringes and a border of blue, supposed to be repentant, he hasn't seen God. He should welcome them, be happy they came: this is my time to get built up and talk to the men who walked with Christ. Instead he won't let them in and tells the brothers not to come back if they go out to them. That's how evil and prideful these demons are. They use good intentions to cover their evil.

precepts.why: “Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall.” That's what happened with that brother. He got prideful and destroyed his own soul. The Lord is going to destroy spirits like that. He acted like he had good intentions, but when the apostles came he wouldn't let them in. Why? He's scared the congregation will follow them, scared he'll lose his following. It's about him, not building up the people's minds and spirits. The people in there are worshipping him. Right behind all that pride, your fall is coming.

sense.text:
“The Lord knoweth the thoughts of man, that they are vanity.” The Lord knows what's in men's minds. Vanity is the quality of being worthless or futile. Futile: incapable of producing any useful result. Brothers are around just to be around, incapable of producing any useful result. You're pointless. We can't depend on you or trust you.

Vain, pointless, useless, unsuccessful, unprofitable, doomed, hopeless, ineffectual, ineffective, no use, unproductive, impotent, idle, valueless, hollow, empty, sterile. Those are the words. The Lord knows men's thoughts are vanity.

“heard of the valiant acts and warlike deeds which they had done.” Joseph and Azarias heard what Judas and Jonathan were doing. “Let us also get us a name”. Let us be like them and get a name. “and go fight against the heathen that are round about us.” We're going to fight the heathen and do like Judas was doing.
“So when they had given charge unto the garrison that was with them”. The garrison was a group of men; they had thousands of men following their foolishness.

“Joseph and Azaras were put to flight”. Nobody told them to go out and fight. The Lord put the spirit on Judas, Jonathan, and the brothers, not on them to go out there. They wanted to make a name for themselves under the guise of good intentions, just going out to destroy the people. “there were slain that day of the people of Israel about two thousand men.” Two thousand men got slain because they tried to do a mighty deed under the guise of good intentions.

“because they were not obedient unto Judas and his brethren”. They were self-willed. They didn't want to follow the men before them. The same thing happens in this truth: men want to recreate the wheel and make their own blueprint when the blueprint is laid out already. The Lord put the spirit on the men who came before them. Our job is to follow orders, follow the men set before us, and the Lord will bless us.

Trying to make your own name and do your own thing gets people hurt. Two thousand men got put to death. We had good intentions to fight our enemy—but God didn't send you out there. “but thought to do some valiant act.”

precepts.why: “There is a way that seemeth right unto a man, but the end thereof are the ways of death.” It seems right to go do it, but it ends in death. We cannot play with God or this Bible. We can't use good intents to do evil works or cover foolishness. We have to learn to follow orders in this truth and follow what the Most High set before us.

sense.text: “Up, make us gods, which shall go before us”. Moses didn't come down from the mountain right away, so Aaron made golden calves under good intentions: I'm just making a god for them. No, he knew that was evil and idolatry. He was a priest; he knew better. “These be thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.” God just brought us out of Egypt, and now they're saying these calves are our gods.

“the people sat down to eat and to drink, and rose up to play.” They were fornicating, committing adultery and idolatry, reveling and partying, the same thing they're doing in the churches. All type of evil was going on among our forefathers.

“it is a stiffnecked people”. We ain't changed yet. The bulk of us are still stiffnecked. “let me alone, that my wrath may wax hot against them”. The Lord is mad as hell because they're saying cows are our gods, a golden calf that can't do anything for them brought them out of Egypt. They got that from Egypt.

“Wherefore should the Egyptians speak, and say, For mischief did he bring them out”. Moses is telling the Lord not to destroy us; the Egyptians will laugh and say he brought us out for nothing. Moses is talking to him face to face, trying to calm him down. Lord, you're mad as hell right now, but don't forget your promises to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

“Remember Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, thy servants”. “I will multiply your seed as the stars of heaven”. Remember the promise that their seed would inherit the land forever.

“And the Lord repented of the evil which he thought to do unto his people.” The Lord calmed down. All right, Moses, you're right; I promised I wouldn't destroy them. He was up there giving Moses righteous laws for us to live by, to make us special people and his children, and we were down there worshipping a calf, having sex, fornication, adultery, and all type of evil. He was mad. He still killed 23,000, but he didn't kill the whole nation of Israel.

“Oh, this people have sinned a great sin, and have made them gods of gold.” Moses was going in on them, not playing with them, slaying them. “blot me, I pray thee, out of thy book which thou hast written.” You know how heavy that is? Lord, blot me out of the book; just keep the promise you made to them. That's the mindset we're supposed to have for our people.

“Whosoever hath sinned against me, him will I blot out of my book.” I ain't going to blot you out, Moses. Whoever broke my laws and disobeyed me, that's the one I'm putting to death and taking out of the book of life.

“nevertheless in the day when I visit I will visit their sin upon them.” I ain't going to forget what they did, Moses. I'm going to hold it against them. “And the Lord plagued the people, because they made the calf, which Aaron made.” That's how he plagued them: he killed 23,000. He wasn't playing with us. Aaron did it under the guise of good intentions, but it was terrible judgment to make golden calves when the Lord had just brought us out of Egypt and set him up as priest.

precepts.why: “But with many of them God was not well pleased: for they were overthrown in the wilderness.” “Now these things were our examples, to the intent we should not lust after evil things”. That whole thing happened as an example so we wouldn't lust after evil things as our forefathers did. “Neither be ye idolaters, as were some of them”. They had those calves and were idolatrous. “The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play.” Fornication, reveling, idolatry—all type of evil was going on. “Neither let us commit fornication, as some of them committed, and fell in one day three and twenty thousand.” Twenty-three thousand people fell in the wilderness, put to death for that foolishness.

“I am the Lord your God.” “After the doings of the land of Egypt, wherein ye dwelt, shall ye not do”. “and after the doings of the land of Canaan, whither I bring you, shall ye not do: neither shall ye walk in their ordinances.” Don't follow what they do. Our forefathers came out of Egypt following the garbage they followed there. That's why they made the golden calves; that's what they knew. As soon as Moses disappeared, we went right back to the evil our slave masters had us doing.

sense.text: “Ananias, with Sapphira his wife, sold a possession”. “And kept back part of the price, his wife also being privy to it”. She knew about it. She knew what he was doing when he brought a certain part and laid it at the apostles' feet.

“Whiles it remained, was it not thine own?” It was yours. You didn't have to lie about how much you sold the land for. “and after it was sold, was it not in thine own power?” It was in your power to give what you wanted, but you lied for no reason. “thou hast not lied unto men, but unto God.” “And Ananias hearing these words fell down, and gave up the ghost”. He dropped dead right there.

He had good intentions to sell a house and give proceeds to the Lord, but he lied to Peter for no reason. Good intentions ended with terrible judgment. Remember that when we're running around lying for little or nothing. The Most High can make us drop dead right there like he did them. Everything in the Bible is for our example, for us to learn how to live today.

“when his wife, not knowing what was done, came in.” She didn't know her husband had dropped dead. “Tell me whether ye sold the land for so much?” What did you sell the land for, sis? “Yea, for so much.” Yes, we sold it for that much.

“How is it that ye have agreed together to tempt the Spirit of the Lord?” It was their property, their proceeds, their offering to help out, but they lied about it for no reason. The Lord didn't play that. “behold, the feet of them which have buried thy husband are at the door, and shall carry thee out.” “Then fell she down straightway at his feet, and yielded up the ghost”.

“And great fear came upon all the church, and upon as many as heard these things.” The Lord used them as an example to put fear on the rest of the church about dealing falsely, deceit, and lying about little or nothing. What did they have to lie about when it was their own property they were giving? Don't play games with him.

“They shall put you out of the synagogues”. Out of the churches. “yea, the time cometh, that whosoever killeth you will think that he doeth God service.” It happened back then, and it's going to happen in these days. These Christians are going to get mad because they can't defend their gospel anymore. Everything they come out with, God is cornering them off. What comes next? Violence. Let's put them to death. They're lying. They're false prophets. They're going to kill us because they can't defend their gospel anymore, thinking they're doing a good thing, thinking they have good intentions.

“because they have not known the Father, nor me.” They never knew God, Christ, or this Bible. They're mad, the spirit of Satan is on them, and they'll put us to death thinking they're doing right because they can't back up what they're saying anymore.

“But these things have I told you”. We have a true and living God who warns us before these things happen. “that when the time shall come, ye may remember that I told you” Remember he warned us they'd kill us thinking they were doing the right thing, having good intentions.

“sorrow hath filled your heart.” He warned the disciples, the men around him, what was going to happen. Sorrow filled their hearts because they knew these people would put them to death thinking they were doing right.

“Hear now, ye rebels; must we fetch you water out of this rock?” The Lord didn't tell Moses to say that. Moses was so mad he took it upon himself. He's mad as hell at them. Must we? He included himself with the Most High.
“with his rod he smote the rock twice”. He hit the rock twice.

See, when you're doing something good, it make it okay if you do something bad, it like even itself out. He's saying that like you do something good just in case when you do something bad, it can even itself out.

Oh, that's what some of y'all in here do. You work out a whole day. Now y'all can feel like you can go stop at Dunkin Donuts and get you some donuts or whatever to go eat.

I gave $10 to God, so now I can go spend $1,000 on some foolishness I don't even need. You understand? That's what they do. That's what they talking about. I could give God $10 to say I gave him something, but I go spend $1,000 on something I don't even need. You understand what I'm saying? All type of Tik Tok products and all that. You buying all of Tik Tok and you don't need it. House full of supplies that you don't even need. You ain't going to be able to use it. But you make yourself feel good when you do that. You understand?

So you do what? You trick yourself to think one good deed cancel another. Cancel out a bad one. Hey, you start bending the rules. You start being deceitful. You start doing things you don't normally do because why? Now you can say, 'I'm doing it under good intentions.' That's when moral licensing coming back to. It don't give you a free pass.

That's what you got to question yourself. You understand what I'm saying? A lot of people use good intentions to do evil. You understand? Or do wrong things or not hold themselves accountable or not hold themselves responsible for things they supposed to be doing. You understand? They use that one good deed to do evil.

“Because ye believed me not, to sanctify me in the eyes of the children of Israel”. The Lord was supposed to be sanctified, but Moses got so mad he said, shall we? It was supposed to be shall he, so the Lord could be glorified. “therefore ye shall not bring this congregation into the land which I have given them.” Moses wasn't making it across into that land because he included himself with the Most High. Even with his good character, that mistake, that deed he did, made the Most High mad as hell.

“but there is some that counselleth for himself.” Be careful. Some people act like they're doing a good deed by talking and counselling with you, but they're counselling for themselves. “Beware of a counsellor”. Be cautious. You're supposed to come to the table, to the leaders of the church. Instead, you're talking to a brother who's been here damn eight months, or you've been here a year and are giving somebody counsel on the low. You don't fully understand judgment yet. You're supposed to send him up to the leaders of the school.

Well, I was just talking to him. No, you was counselling him. What the hell are you talking about, just talking to him? Good intentions is what they're using. “and know before what need he hath”. Know what he needs; some men will counsel for themselves.

“Thy way is good”. He'll tell you what you're talking about is good. “and afterward he stand on the other side, to see what shall befall thee.” When you get in trouble, he steps aside like he never said anything. Let me see if they're going to blast him. If they don't, it's all right; if they do, he won't step up and say he told you or spoke to you. That good deed, that good intention to tell you something, leaves you alone when you get in trouble. Be cautious about who you talk to and whose advice you take.

“Consult not with one that suspecteth thee: and hide thy counsel from such as envy thee.” Some people counsel for themselves. They act like they're doing right, but when you get in trouble they'll back up off you.

“And Jephthah vowed a vow unto the Lord”. He wanted to do a valiant act and prayed to the Lord about it. “whatsoever cometh forth of the doors of my house to meet me, when I return in peace from the children of Ammon”. Lord, the first thing that comes out of my house when I return safely from destroying the Ammonites, I'll give to you. “and I will offer it up for a burnt offering.”
“and the Lord delivered them into his hands.” The Lord gave him the victory he prayed for.

“his daughter came out to meet him with timbrels and with dances”. The first thing out of his house was his daughter. She was happy he won the battle and ran out to meet him. “and she was his only child”. Remember the vow: whatever came out first, he'd sacrifice to the Lord. This was his only child; he had neither another son nor daughter.

“for I have opened my mouth unto the Lord, and I cannot go back.” He opened his mouth and couldn't take it back. When you vow a vow, you have to keep it. He had good intentions: win the battle for Israel and come home safely in peace. But the first thing out of his house was his daughter, his only child. She went away for a couple of months, came back, and he had to keep his vow.

He didn't expect his daughter to come running out. He meant well, but those good intentions didn't work out well for him. A bad outcome, a bad result, bad judgment. Our forefathers did things with good intentions, and some of the results turned out bad. Ninety percent of the time good intentions are bad judgments.

“And David and all Israel played before God with all their might, and with singing”. David called for the ark of the covenant to come out. They're bringing it out, happy, singing, dancing, having a good time glorifying the Lord with the ark.

“Uzza put forth his hand to hold the ark; for the oxen stumbled.” The ark was shaking, and he put his hand out to stop it falling. “And the anger of the Lord was kindled against Uzza”. Only the priests, Aaron's sons, could deal with the ark. Only the high priest could touch it, Aaron and his sons. He did something he wasn't supposed to do. Good intentions, poor judgment.

“and he smote him, because he put his hand to the ark: and there he died before God.” He died because he touched it. Sometimes it's a knee-jerk reaction: something is falling, and you go to stop it. But he knew he wasn't supposed to touch it. The Lord told all Israel we can't touch the ark of the covenant; only the high priest could touch it. He had good intentions, but the result was terrible. He got put to death.

“And David was afraid of God that day”. David got scared to death. Imagine somebody touching a damn ark and dropping dead right there on the spot. That's scary. The Lord ain't playing. I don't care if you have good intentions. If he says don't do it, don't do it. Some of our forefathers had great intentions and bad outcomes. For some people 'I meant well, I had good will, it was in my heart to help' is just a backup in case they do wrong.

“Nadab and Abihu, the sons of Aaron, took either of them his censer, and put fire therein”. These are high priests. They put the fire in the censers and incense on it. “and offered strange fire before the Lord, which he commanded them not.” He didn't command them to make that fire.
“And there went out fire from the Lord, and devoured them”. Fire shot out from the Lord, and he killed them. “and they died before the Lord.”

“And Aaron held his peace.” Aaron shut the hell up. He had nothing to say about what the Lord did because they were sacrificing to strange gods, putting strange fire. The Lord made fire shoot out and burnt their behinds up. They were supposed to be the high priests. Setting up incense wasn't out of the ordinary, but they were burning strange fire.
“this do ye, as oft as ye drink it, in remembrance of me.” As often as we drink it, we're supposed to remember Christ.

“Wherefore whosoever shall eat this bread, and drink this cup of the Lord, unworthily, shall be guilty of the body and blood of the Lord.” We go through this every week, and brothers still go out committing adultery, fornication, lying, stealing, dealing falsely and deceitfully. They might be idol worshipping, sneaking and celebrating Thanksgiving or Christmas after leaving the school. We have the getaway on those days; they come in the daytime and then go to their families to celebrate those wicked holidays.

Some people break this bread unworthily without considering the damage the Lord can do to them for going out and committing evil. These things keep coming up back to back. The righteous fall and get back up, but some people are in the midst of evil for a long time, not taking this truth seriously. They take the law and breaking bread for granted, then go do evil right away with no fear of the Lord. They have good intentions, but the spirit is strong and the flesh is weak.
“But let a man examine himself”. That's what we're supposed to do in here: examine whether we're walking in the faith and whether we're sincere.
“eateth and drinketh damnation to himself, not discerning the Lord’s body.” You're sinning against your own soul when you break that bread and go out and do evil, not dealing with Christ.
“For this cause many are weak and sickly among you”. That's why a lot among us get weak and sickly. “and many sleep.” Many get put to death.

“For if we would judge ourselves, we should not be judged.” If we judge ourselves, we shouldn't have to be judged. Know what you're supposed to do and walk right. Don't come in here talking about good intentions when you're not doing right. We're supposed to change our minds and spirits, get out of that world, conform to this Bible, and come back to being the righteous people we really are, new children in Christ.

This isn't time to play. Heavy, hard times are coming in these last days. We have to be sincere around each other, loyal to the Lord, able to trust one another. Remember why you walked through those doors: you wanted change, to learn about the Lord, the kingdom of heaven, immortality, a righteous life. Don't hold on to the old man and say you're trying to do right. Just do it.
“and fell among thieves, which stripped him of his raiment, and wounded him”. They beat the hell out of him and robbed him, leaving him half dead.

“there came down a certain priest that way”. The high priest, the man of God, came that way. “and when he saw him, he passed by on the other side.” He saw the man laid out, went to the other side, and kept walking. “And likewise a Levite”. Come on, Levi, get your spirit right. “came and looked on him, and passed by on the other side.” Levi, you got holier than thou, went to the other side, and kept walking.

“But a certain Samaritan, as he journeyed, came where he was”. So, you had Judah and Levi walk past him. You had Judah and Levi walk past him. But then, uh then uh you had this good Samaritan. “and when he saw him, he had compassion on him”. Be compassionate on the brother. He bound his wounds, poured in oil and wine, put him on his own beast, and brought him to an inn. “and took care of him.”

“he took out two pence, and gave them to the host, and said unto him, Take care of him”. He gave him money: take care of this brother. Somebody beat the hell out of him and robbed him. “and whatsoever thou spendest more, when I come again, I will repay thee.” Any more costs you have for him, I'll give it to you when I get back.

“Which now of these three, thinkest thou, was neighbour unto him that fell among the thieves?” Which one was really his neighbour? “He that shewed mercy on him.” “Go, and do thou likewise.” Go do the same thing. Help your brother. Don't just think about yourself in this walk. Care for your brother, your sister, and your people more than yourself.

Altruism is selfless concern for the well-being of others, without care for one's own interest. Care for other brothers, the congregation, and our people. America destroyed a lot of our people and made them think only about themselves. Young men and women don't think about how what they do reflects on their family, household, or the whole organization. We're supposed to be changed men with a different mind and way of processing things. No more I, me; it's we, us, our. All through the Bible and Paul's letters it's about the people, not the individual. Self-preservation was how we thought in the world. In this truth we have to rely on and trust one another.

Unselfishness, selflessness, self-sacrifice, self-denial. Some work with vulnerable elderly people out of altruism. It's hard for Israel to understand not thinking about ourselves; we have to think about our nation day in and day out. If you do evil and somebody sees you, you embarrass the whole nation, not just yourself or your household. Goodwill, kindness, compassion, generosity, charity, humanitarianism. That's the mindset. A lot of people hide behind good intentions as a backup for evil and unrighteousness.
“as Debora my father’s mother had commanded me, because I was left an orphan by my father.” Tobit was an orphan. His grandmother told him how to give alms and take care of his business.

“if I saw any of my nation dead, or cast about the walls of Nineve, I buried him.” He walked around burying the dead, looking out for his people. “And if the king Sennacherib had slain any, when he was come, and fled from Judea, I buried them privily”. He saw the bodies, picked them up, and made sure he put them in the ground.

“Then all my goods were forcibly taken away”. All his goods were taken for doing right, for not thinking about himself. “neither was there any thing left me, beside my wife Anna and my son Tobias.” All he had left was his wife and son, for running around doing great works, burying Israel instead of letting their bodies lie in the streets.
“Epaphroditus, my brother, and companion in labour, and fellowsoldier”. “and he that ministered to my wants.” Epaphroditus helped Paul out and ministered to his wants.

“For he longed after you all, and was full of heaviness”. He loved you all. “because that ye had heard that he had been sick.” He got really sick. Like when we go on these trips: sometimes the bishop, deacons, captains, or officers get sick, but we're out there doing the work. “For indeed he was sick nigh unto death: but God had mercy on him”. God had mercy because he was doing the work.

“Receive him therefore in the Lord with all gladness; and hold such in reputation”. He put his life on the line to serve them, to help Paul get to these people and build them up. He almost died from sickness doing the work. “Because for the work of Christ he was nigh unto death”. All of us in the nation of Israel should have that mindset to do Christ's work, even when it comes down to sickness. We still have to get the work done.

“not regarding his life, to supply your lack of service toward me.” He didn't regard his own life in doing what Paul asked. To hell with it, I'm still going. I'm not feeling a hundred; I'm still going.
“The Spirit of the Lord is upon me”. The spirit of the Lord was upon him.
“To preach the acceptable year of the Lord.” To preach the return of the Lord.

“Is not this Joseph’s son?” After all that good stuff and those good scriptures, they turn around and say, ain't that Joseph and Mary's son? How is he talking like this now? They didn't just hear the words and get excited that he came to preach, heal the brokenhearted, and do wonderful healings. The first thing they say is, is that Joseph's son?
“whatsoever we have heard done in Capernaum, do also here in thy country.” They heard of his works over there and hoped he'd do them here, but they weren't showing Christ any love in his own country.
“And Judas also, which betrayed him, knew the place”. We have to be mindful. Judas knew their secret hideout, where they used to go with the disciples.
“Whom seek ye?” Who are you looking for? “Jesus of Nazareth.” “I am he.” “they went backward, and fell to the ground.” All of them went backwards.

“I have told you that I am he”. He was flexing on them. I told you I'm him. “if therefore ye seek me, let these go their way”. “Of them which thou gavest me have I lost none.” Christ stood up for his people. None of them got lost; he made sure none of the disciples got taken away.

“Then Simon Peter having a sword drew it, and smote the high priest’s servant, and cut off his right ear.” Peter wanted to do a good deed, pulled out the knife, and cut his ear off. “The servant’s name was Malchus.” “Put up thy sword into the sheath: the cup which my Father hath given me, shall I not drink it?”

Christ did a good deed making sure none of the disciples got taken away. Peter came around trying to do a heroic act and cut the dude's ear off. Don't you understand I have to drink this cup? Peter didn't understand. He was trying to stop the mission through his good deed, and that good deed turned out to be a bad result.

“And there are also many other things which Jesus did”. Christ looked out for our people, died for our people, healed our people, and fed our people. “I suppose that even the world itself could not contain the books that should be written.” The books couldn't contain all the wonderful works Christ did for his nation.

Ninety percent of the time those good intentions end up being bad results, bad judgment, bad decisions. A lot of times they're a cover for evil work, for not completing the task, not doing what's needed, or keeping an escape route ready when you fail. Be mindful when a brother says he has good intentions.
